A298173.name: Solution (a(n)) of the complementary equation in Comments.
comment: Define sequences a(n) and b(n) recursively, starting with a(0) = 1, b(0) = 2:
b(n) = least new;
where "least new k" means the least positive integer not yet placed, and x(k) = (-1)^k for k >= 0.
It appears that a(n)/a(n-1) -> 3 and that {a(n) - 3*a(n-1), n >= 1} is unbounded.
A298173.author: _Clark Kimberling_, May 12 2018

A298741.name: Solution (a(n)) of the complementary equation in Comments.
comment: Define sequences a(n) and b(n) recursively, starting with a(0) = 1, b(0) = 2:
b(n) = least new;
where "least new k" means the least positive integer not yet placed, x(0) = 2, and x(k) = (-1)^k for k >= 1.
It appears that a(n)/a(n-1) -> 2 and that {a(n) - 2*a(n-1), n >=1 } is unbounded.
A298741.author: _Clark Kimberling_, May 12 2018

A305129.name: Solution (a(n)) of the complementary equation a(n) = 2*a(n-1) - a(n-2) + b(n); see Comments.
comment: Define sequences a(n) and b(n) recursively, starting with a(0) = 1, a(1) = 2:
b(n) = least new;

where "least new" means the least positive integer not yet placed.  It appears that a(n)/a(n-1) -> 1, that {a(n) - a(n-1), n>=1} is unbounded, and that the 3rd difference sequence of (a(n)) consists entirely of 1's and 2's.
link: Clark Kimberling, Table of n, a(n) for n = 0..10000
A305129.author: _Clark Kimberling_, May 30 2018
